headline: NEW IN-WINDOW -- Ansar Allah (Ansar Allah) call for immediate evacuation of Aden airport, alleging a Saudi weapons cargo plane is
dek: Ansar Allah called on everyone at Aden airport -- seat of the Saudi-backed internationally recognised government -- to evacuate immediately, alleging a Saudi military cargo plane carrying weapons was present 'to kill the sons of the Yemeni people' (Saree, Telegram/X). Residents told Reuters…
sources: Yahya Saree (Ansar Allah military spokesman) post on Telegram/X, reported by Reuters and AFP
fault_line: Is Aden airport a legitimate military target because of an alleged weapons plane, or a humanitarian lifeline whose evacuation warning is itself the escalation?

sections.what_happened: Ansar Allah called on everyone at Aden airport -- seat of the Saudi-backed internationally recognised government -- to evacuate immediately, alleging a Saudi military cargo plane carrying weapons was present 'to kill the sons of the Yemeni people' (Saree, Telegram/X). Residents told Reuters explosions were heard in Aden before the warning. No immediate Saudi comment. Aden airport has been struck repeatedly in recent weeks and is described by Reuters as a humanitarian lifeline and gateway to southern Yemen. Context: government forces recently retook Red Sea coastal territory, loosening Ansar Allah's grip near Bab el-Mandeb; the 2022 UN truce is shattered; Al Mayadeen/Saba also report Saudi strikes on al-Hazm market (al-Jawf) with a preliminary toll rising to 11 killed, 10 injured -- that toll is single-source (Saba via Al Mayadeen) and NOT adopted here.
sections.what_verified: Three distinct declared-tier families: Reuters (T1, via Straits Times/GMA/Business Recorder/Oman Observer carries), AFP (T1, via Deccan Chronicle), Times of Israel (T3, liveblog carry of the Saree Telegram post). The evacuation call is identical across all three; the weapons-plane claim originates with Saree alone.
sections.what_disputed: No Saudi comment retrieved; the weapons-plane claim is unverified and serves as the stated pretext for a strike warning. Explosions heard in Aden are resident reports to Reuters, cause unattributed. Al-Hazm casualty toll (11 killed) rests on Saba via Al Mayadeen alone and is not corroborated in this record.
sections.why_matters: 'Evacuate Aden airport NOW' -- the warning that precedes a strike: map the airport, the Bab el-Mandeb lane, and what a hit does to southern Yemen's lifeline.
sections.context: Background: NEW IN-WINDOW -- Ansar Allah (Ansar Allah) call for immediate evacuation of Aden airport, alleging a Saudi weapons cargo plane is present; explosions heard in Aden before the warning (Reuters/AFP, Oct 28)

totw_analysis: Our read: 'Evacuate Aden airport NOW' -- the warning that precedes a strike: map the airport, the Bab el-Mandeb lane, and what a hit does to southern Yemen's lifeline. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Aden airport a legitimate military target because of an alleged weapons plane, or a humanitarian lifeline whose evacuation warning is itself the escalation?
